set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which variant of granuloma annulare carries the strongest systemic associations?
opts: Localised disease, which predominates at about 75% of cases and affects children and young adults
Localised disease accounts for about 75% of cases and is asymptomatic.
Subcutaneous, occurring almost exclusively in children under six
This variant may mimic rheumatoid nodules but lacks those systemic links.
Perforating, with central umbilication and extrusion of collagen
This variant may scar but is not the one with systemic associations.
Generalised or disseminated, associated with diabetes, thyroid disease, dyslipidaemia and lymphoma
Correct, and it is more common in adults over forty.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What does the lecture say about patients with Fitzpatrick types IV to VI?
opts: They are not immune to ultraviolet damage or skin cancer, and melanoma is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages
Correct — delayed diagnosis is common because of a lower index of suspicion.
They carry no meaningful skin cancer risk and need no routine photoprotection
Risk is lower but explicitly not absent.
They burn more readily than types I to III but tan more deeply afterwards
Types IV to VI burn minimally or never.
They should use SPF 15 rather than SPF 30, on the basis that higher factors confer no additional benefit
The guidance is broad-spectrum SPF 30 or above for daily use across all types.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What causes epidermolysis bullosa?
opts: Autoantibodies against the epidermal basement membrane
That is bullous pemphigoid.
A mutation in structural proteins
Correct — the level at which the skin separates follows from which protein is affected.
Immunoglobulin A deposition in the dermal papillae
That is dermatitis herpetiformis.
A type IV hypersensitivity reaction to a drug
That is Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How broad is the referral requirement in epidermolysis bullosa?
opts: Essentially every specialty, given the multisystem burden
Correct — palliative care, genetics and family support are all involved.
Dermatology alone, since the disease is confined to the skin
The disease burden is multisystem.
Genetics alone, since the diagnosis is made on a genetic panel
Genetics is one referral among many.
No routine referral, since the condition is managed in primary care
The condition requires broad specialist involvement.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How does polymorphous light eruption typically present?
opts: Painful erythema developing within minutes of ultraviolet exposure and resolving within an hour of moving into the shade
That immediate pattern suggests solar urticaria.
An exaggerated sunburn on first exposure to a new medication
That describes phototoxicity.
Persistent eczematous change in chronically exposed skin of older males
That describes chronic actinic dermatitis.
Papules appearing thirty minutes to hours after exposure on the décolletage, forearms and dorsal hands, sparing chronically exposed skin
Correct, resolving in seven to ten days without scarring and recurring each spring.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Why does azelaic acid need care in rosacea despite being effective?
opts: It is contraindicated in pregnancy because of teratogenic risk
That caution belongs to oral isotretinoin.
It raises intraocular pressure with prolonged facial application
That caution belongs to topical corticosteroids.
It is more drying, and these patients already have an impaired skin barrier and dry skin
Correct — that is why metronidazole is preferred first.
It causes marked photosensitivity, so daily sun protection becomes mandatory
Photosensitivity is not the caution given for this agent here.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the mortality of toxic epidermal necrolysis, and what predicts it at presentation?
opts: Up to 30 to 35%, predicted by the SCORTEN score calculated within 24 hours
Correct, and SCORTEN is repeated on day three.
Between 1 and 5%, predicted by the extent of mucosal involvement
That mortality figure belongs to Stevens-Johnson syndrome alone.
Under 1%, predicted by the number of drugs the patient was taking
Toxic epidermal necrolysis carries substantially higher mortality than this.
Around 50%, predicted by the presence of the Nikolsky sign
The Nikolsky sign is present across the spectrum and is not a prognostic score.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What triggers the majority of erythema multiforme cases?
opts: Mycoplasma pneumoniae, accounting for over 50% of cases
Mycoplasma is a recognised infectious trigger but not the leading one.
Idiopathic causes, accounting for over 50% of cases
Idiopathic causes account for roughly 10% of cases.
Herpes simplex virus, accounting for over 50% of cases
Correct. Other infectious causes include Mycoplasma pneumoniae, histoplasmosis, Epstein-Barr virus and coxsackievirus.
Sulfonamide antibiotics, accounting for over 50% of cases
Drugs including sulfonamides are triggers, but they are far from the majority.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What mechanism underlies the most common form of acanthosis nigricans?
opts: Autoantibody deposition along the epithelial basement membrane zone
That mechanism produces bullous pemphigoid.
Hyperinsulinaemia stimulating keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation through insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor cross-activation
Correct — the insulin-resistant or benign form is the commonest.
A paraneoplastic process driven by an underlying gastric adenocarcinoma secreting growth factors that act on the epidermis
Malignant acanthosis nigricans is rare, at under 1% of cases.
A delayed type IV hypersensitivity reaction to a contacted allergen
That mechanism produces allergic contact dermatitis.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which measures are named for acute sunburn?
opts: Silver sulfadiazine dressings applied twice daily under occlusion
That is a burn dressing agent not used in ordinary sunburn.
Cool compresses, an early nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug, and oral hydration
Correct — ibuprofen or naproxen reduce the prostaglandin-mediated pain.
Warm compresses, an oral antihistamine, and a topical corticosteroid cream
Warm compresses are used for furuncles and paronychia.
Ice packs applied directly, with a systemic corticosteroid taper
Cool rather than cold is advised, and steroids are not part of this.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the principal risk a patient must understand before endoscopic thoracic sympathectomy?
opts: Compensatory sweating elsewhere, occurring in over 30%
Correct — the procedure is permanent, so the trade-off has to be discussed thoroughly beforehand.
The need for retreatment every three to six months
That applies to botulinum toxin rather than sympathectomy.
Dry mouth and urinary retention as ongoing side effects
Those are the anticholinergic effects of oral therapy.
Permanent destruction of axillary glands by microwave energy
That describes microwave thermolysis rather than sympathectomy.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which biologic is approved for refractory chronic urticaria?
opts: Dupilumab, an interleukin-4 receptor antagonist given subcutaneously
Dupilumab has been reported in refractory granuloma annulare rather than approved here.
Etanercept, a tumour necrosis factor inhibitor given subcutaneously
Etanercept is described as an emerging adjunct in Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Omalizumab, an anti-immunoglobulin E antibody given every four weeks
Correct, at 300 mg subcutaneously.
Infliximab, a tumour necrosis factor alpha inhibitor given intravenously
Infliximab is approved for pyoderma gangrenosum in inflammatory bowel disease.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is pyoderma gangrenosum, despite its name?
opts: A neutrophilic dermatosis that is not infectious
Correct — dysregulated innate immune activation with neutrophil recruitment causes the tissue destruction.
A deep bacterial infection requiring prolonged antibiotics
The name is misleading; wound cultures are obtained precisely to exclude infection.
A vasculitis of medium-sized vessels with immune complex deposition
Vasculitis is among the differentials that must be excluded.
A malignant ulcerating tumour of keratinocyte origin
Squamous cell carcinoma is a differential requiring biopsy to exclude.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What must be checked before starting dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: Thyroid-stimulating hormone and anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies
Autoimmune thyroid disease is an association but is not the pre-treatment check.
Serum immunoglobulin A level to exclude selective deficiency
This affects serological interpretation rather than dapsone safety.
HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 typing to confirm susceptibility
Typing is used when serology is equivocal rather than before dapsone.
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase status
Correct, and the blood count is then monitored for haemolytic anaemia and methaemoglobinaemia.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How is a positive photopatch test interpreted?
opts: Any reaction indicates phototoxicity regardless of which patch responds
The test is designed specifically to separate photoallergy from contact allergy.
A reaction only on the irradiated patch indicates photoallergy; a reaction on both indicates contact allergy
Correct — the suspected photohaptens are applied in duplicate and one set irradiated with ultraviolet A.
A reaction on both patches indicates photoallergy; a reaction on one indicates phototoxicity
Reaction on both patches indicates ordinary contact allergy.
A reaction on the non-irradiated patch alone indicates photoallergy
That result would indicate contact allergy independent of light.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which epidermolysis bullosa subtype carries the highest mortality?
opts: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita, the autoimmune acquired form
This acquired form is autoimmune rather than genetic and is not the highest-mortality type.
Junctional epidermolysis bullosa, especially the Herlitz subtype
Correct, which is why early palliative care integration is appropriate in severe Herlitz disease.
Epidermolysis bullosa simplex, especially the localised palmoplantar form
Simplex disease is localised to palms and soles and heals without scarring.
Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, especially the dominant form
Dystrophic disease causes severe scarring and squamous cell carcinoma risk rather than the highest mortality.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What causes phytophotodermatitis, and how does it present?
opts: Furanocoumarins in plants such as lime, celery and parsley plus ultraviolet A, producing linear streaked hyperpigmentation
Correct — classically after lime juice and sun exposure, with painful blistering acutely.
Bergapten in bergamot oil used in fragrances and cosmetics, producing drip-pattern hyperpigmentation of the neck
That describes berloque dermatitis, a separate subtype.
A persistent eczematous eruption in chronically exposed skin of older males
That describes chronic actinic dermatitis.
A delayed hypersensitivity response to an ultraviolet-induced photoantigen
That describes polymorphous light eruption.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which human leukocyte antigen haplotypes are strongly associated with dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: HLA-B*15:02 and HLA-B*58:01
Those are the severe cutaneous drug reaction associations.
HLA-B27 and HLA-DR4
Those are associated with other rheumatological conditions.
HLA-Cw6 and HLA-DR3
HLA-Cw6 is associated with early-onset psoriasis.
HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8
Correct — the same haplotypes that underlie coeliac disease.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Where is the eruption of dermatitis herpetiformis distributed?
opts: On the anterior shins bilaterally as tender nodules that do not ulcerate
That is erythema nodosum.
On the face in the central third, sparing the nasolabial folds
That is a lupus butterfly rash, which she said she is not testing.
On sun-exposed skin, sparing the chronically exposed face and hands
That is polymorphous light eruption.
Symmetrically on the knees, elbows, buttocks and back
Correct — intensely pruritic papules and vesicles that group in a herpetiform pattern.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which services should a patient with Stevens-Johnson syndrome be under?
opts: Intensive care or a burn unit, with dermatology involved
Correct — nasogastric feeding is often needed because mucosal involvement prevents eating.
A general medical ward with dermatology review the following day
That level of care is inadequate for this condition.
Outpatient dermatology with a review appointment in one week
That level of care is inadequate for this condition.
Ambulatory wound care with daily dressing changes at home
That level of care is inadequate for this condition.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which features should raise suspicion of secondary rather than primary hyperhidrosis?
opts: Bilateral palmar sweating that has been present since adolescence
That pattern describes primary focal disease.
Sweating that worsens with anxiety and improves in a cool room
Anxiety exacerbates primary disease without indicating a secondary cause.
Sweating confined to the axillae with a family history of the same
That pattern describes primary focal disease.
Generalised sweating, nocturnal sweating, or an asymmetric distribution
Correct — primary disease is bilateral, focal and absent during sleep.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which molecular event is critical in actinic keratosis?
opts: Overactivation of the hedgehog signalling pathway
That pathway is implicated in basal cell carcinoma.
Loss of keratinocyte adhesion through autoantibody binding
That mechanism produces pemphigus.
Reduced filaggrin production impairing the epidermal barrier
That defect underlies atopic dermatitis.
Ultraviolet-induced mutation of TP53
Correct, and the surrounding normal-looking skin harbours subclinical mutations, called field cancerisation.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A patient has had four episodes of herpes-associated erythema multiforme this year. Which chronic measure is appropriate?
opts: Annual phototherapy given as a five-week course each spring
That is preventive therapy for polymorphous light eruption.
Suppressive antiviral therapy, such as aciclovir 400 mg twice daily
Correct — preventing the herpes recurrence prevents the eruption.
A standing prescription for oral prednisone to take at each episode
Steroid at each episode does not prevent recurrence.
Long-term oral antihistamines taken continuously through the year
Antihistamines address pruritus rather than recurrence.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which single feature most usefully distinguishes erythema nodosum from nodular vasculitis?
opts: Erythema nodosum nodules are painless on palpation
The nodules are tender, which is part of the classic description.
Erythema nodosum nodules occur exclusively in men
There is a female predominance of three to six to one.
Erythema nodosum nodules do not ulcerate
Correct, and they sit on the anterior shins whereas nodular vasculitis favours the posterior legs and ulcerates.
Erythema nodosum nodules appear only on the posterior legs
The anterior shins are the characteristic site.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How is an isolated actinic keratosis usually treated?
opts: Photodynamic therapy using aminolevulinic acid and light
This is excellent for field treatment rather than an isolated lesion.
Cryotherapy with two to three freeze-thaw cycles
Correct — the standard of care for isolated lesions, with shave excision or curettage as alternatives.
5-fluorouracil cream applied for two to four weeks
That is a field-directed treatment for multiple or confluent lesions.
Imiquimod applied twice weekly for sixteen weeks
That is also field-directed rather than lesion-directed.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which drug classes are classic causes of phototoxicity?
opts: Aromatic anticonvulsants, allopurinol and nevirapine
Those are the leading triggers of Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Oral contraceptives, sulfonamides and bromides
Those are drug triggers of erythema nodosum.
Tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, amiodarone and thiazides
Correct, alongside furosemide, voriconazole, some nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and psoralens.
Sunscreen chemicals, sulfonamides and phenothiazines
Those are the classic photoallergens rather than phototoxic agents.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How are Stevens-Johnson syndrome, the overlap state and toxic epidermal necrolysis separated?
opts: By whether the Nikolsky sign is positive or negative at presentation
The Nikolsky sign is positive across the spectrum.
By body surface area of epidermal detachment: under 10%, 10 to 30%, and over 30%
Correct — the same disease spectrum divided by extent of detachment.
By the presence of mucosal involvement, which occurs only in the severe form
Mucosal erosions occur in over 90% of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and are nearly universal in toxic epidermal necrolysis.
By whether the trigger was a drug or an infection in each case
Both share the same causative agents, with drugs predominating.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What single feature most reliably separates urticaria from its differentials?
opts: Lesions appear symmetrically on the palms and soles
That acral distribution is characteristic of erythema multiforme.
Lesions leave residual bruising as they resolve
Residual bruising suggests urticarial vasculitis rather than simple urticaria.
Individual lesions last less than twenty-four hours
Correct — this is called the key diagnostic feature, and lesions persisting beyond it suggest urticarial vasculitis.
Individual lesions are intensely pruritic and blanch under pressure
Both are typical of urticaria but neither separates it from the differentials as reliably.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which feature separates papulopustular rosacea from acne vulgaris?
opts: Rosacea has no comedones
Correct — open or closed comedones point to acne vulgaris instead.
Rosacea produces pustules and acne vulgaris does not
Both produce pustules; the comedones are what differ.
Rosacea occurs only in patients over the age of sixty
Peak onset is between thirty and sixty.
Rosacea spares the central face entirely
Central facial involvement is characteristic of rosacea.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which rosacea complication requires urgent ophthalmology referral?
opts: Persistent central facial erythema unresponsive to topical therapy
This is treated with laser or light therapy rather than urgent referral.
Papules and pustules spreading beyond the central face
This warrants dermatology input rather than urgent ophthalmology.
Ocular rosacea with keratitis, visual symptoms or corneal involvement
Correct — untreated ocular disease risks corneal scarring.
Rhinophyma causing nasal airway narrowing over several years
This is managed by dermatologic or plastic surgery rather than urgently.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is beremagene geperpavec?
opts: A monoclonal antibody given intravenously for junctional epidermolysis bullosa
It is a topical gene therapy rather than an antibody.
An oral small molecule that restores keratin 5 and 14 function
It is a topical gel and does not act on keratin genes.
A non-adherent biological dressing designed for fragile skin
Mepitel and Mepilex are the dressings described; this is a gene therapy.
A topical gene therapy gel approved in 2023 for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
Correct, accessible through dermatology referral centres and gene therapy trials.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which points should the conversation with a hyperhidrosis patient cover?
opts: That it is not about poor hygiene or anxiety, with moisture-wicking clothing suggested and realistic expectations set
Correct — botulinum toxin needs repeating every three to six months and can be cost-prohibitive.
That improved washing and a reduction in stress will resolve all of the sweating within a few months
She was explicit that it is not about hygiene or anxiety.
That a single course of treatment produces a permanent cure
Botulinum toxin lasts three to six months and must be repeated.
That the condition is rare and few treatment options exist
It affects roughly 3 to 5% and has a full treatment ladder.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Why must malignancy and infection be excluded in a rapidly expanding ulcer before treating it as pyoderma gangrenosum?
opts: Because a biopsy cannot be taken once immunosuppression has started
That is not the reason given.
Because the diagnosis is one of exclusion and the immunosuppression used would worsen an infection
Correct — the question to answer is why this ulcer is suddenly expanding.
Because pyoderma gangrenosum is itself a premalignant condition
It is a neutrophilic dermatosis rather than premalignant.
Because antibiotics would become the first-line treatment once an infection is confirmed
The condition is not infectious; antibiotics treat a secondary infection only.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which measure is specifically advised against in the management of sunburn?
opts: Popping blisters, because intact blisters are protective
Correct — cool rather than cold water is also specified.
Starting a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug early in the course
Early nonsteroidals are recommended.
Applying aloe vera or a soy-based topical moisturiser
Those are soothing, though they do not alter healing.
Giving oral or intravenous fluids for systemic symptoms
Hydration is part of management.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which advice is given about blisters in second-degree sunburn?
opts: Apply a high-potency topical corticosteroid directly to them
Topical steroids have limited evidence and may help only within six hours.
Cover them with silver sulfadiazine to prevent colonisation
That agent is specifically avoided in severe cutaneous drug reactions.
Do not pop them, because intact blisters are protective
Correct, with cool compresses and early nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for pain.
Drain them under sterile conditions to reduce infection risk
Intact blisters protect the underlying skin.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which systemic therapy has the strongest current evidence in toxic epidermal necrolysis?
opts: Prophylactic antibiotics covering skin and gut flora
Antibiotic prophylaxis is specifically not recommended.
Cyclosporine at 3 to 5 mg/kg daily, started early
Correct, with intravenous immunoglobulin and etanercept as adjunct options.
Intravenous immunoglobulin at 1 g/kg daily for three days
This is an adjunct option rather than the strongest evidence base.
High-dose systemic corticosteroids given for the first week
Corticosteroids remain controversial across the spectrum.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which systemic complications are named in toxic epidermal necrolysis?
opts: Neurocutaneous melanosis, hydrocephalus and seizures in early childhood
Those belong to large congenital melanocytic naevi.
Symblepharon alone, with no involvement of any other organ system
Ocular scarring is one complication among many.
Sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, acute kidney injury, electrolyte imbalance, hypovolaemia and gastrointestinal haemorrhage
Correct — survivors also face sicca syndrome, lung disease and psychological trauma.
Acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, acute rheumatic fever and a post-infectious reactive arthritis of the knee
Those follow streptococcal infection.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How is the diagnosis of pyoderma gangrenosum established?
opts: By exclusion, since there is no gold standard test
Correct — biopsy from the ulcer edge shows dense neutrophils and rules out malignancy and infection.
By biopsy showing a pathognomonic palisading granuloma
Palisading granulomas belong to granuloma annulare.
By wound culture growing a characteristic organism
Cultures are obtained to exclude an infectious cause; they are negative in pyoderma gangrenosum.
By serum antibody testing against dermal structural proteins
The condition is not antibody-mediated in that way.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which referral is indicated for generalised granuloma annulare in an older adult?
opts: Ophthalmology, if any ocular symptoms have developed
That referral belongs to rosacea and to severe drug reactions.
Oncology, if lymphoma is suspected
Correct, alongside dermatology for phototherapy or systemic therapy and endocrine workup for diabetes or thyroid disease.
Vascular surgery, if venous reflux is suspected
That referral belongs to stasis dermatitis.
Thoracic surgery, if refractory disease is present
That referral belongs to hyperhidrosis.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What kind of process is erythema nodosum, histologically?
opts: A palisading granuloma around degenerating collagen
That describes granuloma annulare.
A dense neutrophilic infiltrate without organisms
That describes pyoderma gangrenosum.
A septal panniculitis without vasculitis
Correct — the most common form of panniculitis, a delayed hypersensitivity reaction in subcutaneous fat.
A lobular panniculitis with associated vasculitis
That describes nodular vasculitis, or erythema induratum, a differential.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is field cancerisation, and how does it change management?
opts: Clinically normal skin around the lesions harbours subclinical mutations, so multiple or confluent lesions need field-directed therapy
Correct — 5-fluorouracil, imiquimod, tirbanibulin or diclofenac treat the field rather than single lesions.
Lesions spread outward from a single origin, so wide excision is required
That is not what the term describes.
Lesions seed distant sites through lymphatics, so staging is required
Actinic keratosis is an intraepidermal dysplasia, not a metastasising process.
Lesions recur at exactly the same site after treatment, so repeat cryotherapy at regular intervals is the appropriate response
Cryotherapy is lesion-directed; the field concept concerns surrounding skin.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which test is the gold standard for diagnosing dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: Lesional skin biopsy with haematoxylin and eosin showing subepidermal blistering with neutrophils
Histology supports the diagnosis but the immunofluorescence pattern is what settles it.
Serum immunoglobulin A anti-tissue transglutaminase with anti-endomysial antibodies
These serologies support the diagnosis but are not the gold standard.
Small bowel biopsy demonstrating villous atrophy consistent with coeliac disease
Up to 90% show villous atrophy, but that confirms coeliac disease rather than the skin diagnosis.
Perilesional skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence showing granular immunoglobulin A in the dermal papillae
Correct. Immunoglobulin A anti-epidermal transglutaminase is the most specific serological test.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which counselling point is emphasised for acanthosis nigricans?
opts: It responds fully to topical antifungal therapy within several weeks
That would treat tinea versicolor, one of the differentials.
It resolves spontaneously in most patients without any intervention
It reflects an underlying process that must itself be treated.
It is a metabolic warning sign rather than a hygiene problem, and 5 to 10% weight loss improves the findings
Correct — the hygiene misconception is specifically addressed.
It is a benign cosmetic change that carries no systemic implication and requires no further investigation
It is a visible marker of insulin resistance and sometimes of malignancy.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which features separate a fixed drug eruption from erythema multiforme?
opts: It produces wheals that migrate, blanch fully and resolve within twenty-four hours of first appearing
That describes urticaria.
It produces extensive epidermal detachment with mucosal involvement and systemic toxicity
That describes Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.
It produces tender nodules on the anterior shins that never go on to ulcerate
That describes erythema nodosum.
It recurs at the same site, leaves residual hyperpigmentation, and has few lesions without three concentric zones
Correct — the three-zone target is what defines an erythema multiforme lesion.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which haplotypes are strongly associated with dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8
Correct, and nearly all patients have underlying gluten-sensitive enteropathy even when gastrointestinally asymptomatic.
HLA-B*15:02 and HLA-B*58:01
Those are the pharmacogenomic risk alleles for Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
HLA-Cw6 and HLA-B27
Those are associated with psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis.
HLA-A31 and HLA-BW35
Those are the suggested susceptibility haplotypes for granuloma annulare.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A patient's facial erythema could be rosacea or lupus and the picture is unclear. Which test helps, and how should the result be read?
opts: An antinuclear antibody, which helps rule autoimmune disease OUT — a positive result only means more testing is needed
Correct — many things make it positive, so it cannot rule a condition in.
An antinuclear antibody, which rules autoimmune disease IN when positive and needs no further testing
It cannot rule a condition in; a positive means more testing.
A skin biopsy of the malar area, which distinguishes the two definitively
Histological distinction is not what she asks for here.
A potassium hydroxide preparation of the affected facial skin
That would investigate a fungal cause.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the gold standard test for determining the cleavage plane in epidermolysis bullosa?
opts: Serum enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for structural protein antibodies
Inherited epidermolysis bullosa is not antibody-mediated.
Skin biopsy with transmission electron microscopy
Correct, with immunofluorescence antigen mapping used to localise missing or reduced proteins.
Skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence for immunoglobulin G
That distinguishes acquired autoimmune blistering disease rather than mapping the cleavage plane.
Genetic testing of the known structural protein genes
Genetic testing is confirmatory and guides prognosis and counselling.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the expected course of localised granuloma annulare?
opts: Half of cases resolve spontaneously within two years, so watchful waiting is reasonable
Correct — treatment is primarily for cosmesis or discomfort, and there is no malignant potential.
Nearly all cases progress without systemic therapy, so early treatment is essential
Localised disease is benign and self-limiting in about half of patients.
Most cases transform into squamous cell carcinoma if left untreated
There is no malignant potential.
Lesions persist unchanged lifelong and never resolve without intervention
Spontaneous resolution occurs in about half within two years.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What distinguishes solar lentigo from lentigo maligna?
opts: Solar lentigo appears in early childhood; lentigo maligna appears only after the age of seventy
Solar lentigo reflects cumulative exposure, exceeding 90% prevalence in Caucasians over seventy.
Solar lentigo appears on covered skin; lentigo maligna on exposed skin
Solar lentigo occurs on chronically sun-exposed surfaces.
Solar lentigo has uniform pigmentation; lentigo maligna is asymmetric with irregular border and colour
Correct, and dermoscopy is essential — solar lentigo shows finger-like projections and a moth-eaten border.
Solar lentigo is raised and rough; lentigo maligna is flat and smooth
Solar lentigo is a macule without induration or scale.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What drives the commonest, insulin-resistant form of acanthosis nigricans?
opts: Autoimmune destruction of the melanocytes within the affected intertriginous skin
That is vitiligo.
Chronic ultraviolet exposure driving proliferation of the basal layer melanocytes and increased melanin production
That is solar lentigo.
Immunoglobulin A deposition in the dermal papillae activating neutrophils
That is dermatitis herpetiformis.
Hyperinsulinaemia stimulating keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation through insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor cross-activation
Correct. Malignant, drug-induced and endocrine forms make up the rest.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the immunological basis of dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: Immunoglobulin G antibodies against desmoglein between the keratinocytes
That is pemphigus vulgaris.
A T-cell mediated destruction of melanocytes within the affected epidermis
That is vitiligo.
Immunoglobulin A antibodies against epidermal transglutaminase, forming complexes that deposit in the dermal papillae
Correct — complement and neutrophils are then activated, producing subepidermal blisters.
Immunoglobulin G antibodies directed against the epidermal basement membrane zone at the dermal junction
That is bullous pemphigoid.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How much do tanning beds reduce risk compared with natural sun, and how are they classified?
opts: They halve ultraviolet B exposure while delivering the same ultraviolet A dose
No such reduction is described; they are classified as carcinogenic.
They are safer for Fitzpatrick types I and II under supervision
Those types carry the highest risk from any ultraviolet exposure.
They are acceptable if limited to the months outside peak summer
No safe level of tanning is described.
They are not safer at all, and are classified as Group 1 carcinogens
Correct — there is no safe level of tanning.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the most common infectious trigger of erythema nodosum?
opts: Staphylococcus aureus
This organism is not among the named triggers.
Group A Streptococcus
Correct, alongside Yersinia, tuberculosis, coccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis and hepatitis B and C.
Mycoplasma pneumoniae
Mycoplasma is a leading trigger of erythema multiforme rather than erythema nodosum.
Herpes simplex virus
Herpes simplex triggers over half of erythema multiforme cases.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which intervention is described as the single most evidence-supported for photoaging?
opts: Chemical peeling with glycolic or trichloroacetic acid
Peels provide exfoliation and remodelling rather than the strongest evidence base.
Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen at SPF 30 or above
Correct, for both preventing and slowing progression, and beginning in childhood gives maximal lifetime benefit.
Ablative laser resurfacing performed every few years
Laser resurfacing is most effective for rhytids and texture but is not the top-evidence intervention.
Daily topical vitamin C at 10 to 20% concentration
This is an adjunct antioxidant.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which type of epidermolysis bullosa is most common, and what is its cleavage level?
opts: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, at about 70% of cases, with sub-lamina densa cleavage
Dystrophic disease arises from COL7A1 mutations but is not the commonest.
Kindler epidermolysis bullosa, at about 70% of cases, with mixed cleavage planes
Kindler disease is rare and arises from FERMT1 mutation.
Epidermolysis bullosa simplex, at about 70% of cases, with intraepidermal cleavage
Correct — it results from keratin 5 and 14 mutations and is autosomal dominant.
Junctional epidermolysis bullosa, at about 70% of cases, with cleavage in the lamina lucida
Junctional disease carries the highest mortality but is not the commonest.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the hardening phenomenon in polymorphous light eruption?
opts: Loss of pigment in the affected areas after each episode
This is not a described feature.
Improvement through the summer as tolerance develops after repeated exposure
Correct, which is also why prophylactic narrowband ultraviolet B in spring is the most effective preventive strategy.
Thickening and hardening of the skin from repeated scratching of the eruption
That describes lichenification.
Progressive scarring of affected sites over successive seasons
The eruption resolves without scarring.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which single intervention most improves survival in Stevens-Johnson syndrome?
opts: Early administration of intravenous immunoglobulin at 1 g/kg daily for three days
This shows benefit in retrospective studies but is not the intervention with the strongest survival link.
Prophylactic broad-spectrum antibiotics started on admission
Antibiotic prophylaxis is explicitly not recommended; infections are treated when confirmed.
High-dose systemic corticosteroids given throughout the admission
Systemic corticosteroids remain controversial and are avoided in active infection.
Immediate withdrawal of the causative drug, since each day of delay worsens prognosis
Correct — earlier withdrawal is strongly associated with improved survival.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A patient with chronic urticaria is still symptomatic on a standard dose of a non-sedating antihistamine. What comes next?
opts: Stop the antihistamine and start a leukotriene antagonist alone
Stopping the antihistamine is not the described step.
Increase to up to four times the standard dose, and consider adding an H2 blocker
Correct — omalizumab and ciclosporin follow if that fails.
Switch immediately to a long-term oral corticosteroid taken daily
Long-term systemic steroid is not the described escalation.
Switch across to a first-generation sedating antihistamine at standard dose
The escalation is in dose of the non-sedating agent, not a switch back.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which drugs are named as causes of acanthosis nigricans?
opts: Niacin, corticosteroids, oral contraceptives and protease inhibitors
Correct — drug-induced disease sits alongside the insulin-resistant and malignant forms.
Carbamazepine, phenytoin, lamotrigine and allopurinol preparations
Those cause Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.
Doxycycline, ciprofloxacin, amiodarone and the thiazide diuretics
Those cause drug-induced photosensitivity.
Lithium, systemic steroids and acnegenic mineral oil exposure
Those are the drug factors named for acne vulgaris.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which feature separates photodermatitis from seborrhoeic dermatitis on the face?
opts: Photodermatitis involves the nasolabial folds, which seborrhoeic dermatitis spares
That reverses the two.
Photodermatitis produces greasy yellow scale, which seborrhoeic dermatitis lacks
Greasy yellow scale is the seborrhoeic finding.
Photodermatitis is confined to the scalp, which seborrhoeic dermatitis spares
Neither statement is correct.
Photodermatitis spares the nasolabial folds, which seborrhoeic dermatitis involves
Correct — shadowed areas are protected from light.
